context: Keep known agent/service identities as an error and preserve the existing explicit override escape hatch. Add a separate warning channel/diagnostic for any repo-local user.* values, test JSON and human-readable output plus exit status, and add one concise AGENTS.md operational rule. Verify from a temporary repository so the test does not mutate BenchBox/.git/config. Do not rewrite history, edit the shared config, or add an agent Co-Authored-By trailer. The falsifiable gate invokes the real JSON CLI with process-local Git config injection; the regression guard calls the existing helper with its supported project-only signature.
description: Add a visible, non-fatal audit warning whenever the shared repository config contains any repo-local user.name or user.email, while retaining a fatal finding for known agent/service identities. Document that agents must not write user.* into the shared clone and must use per-command git -c identity overrides. The guard is detection and instruction hardening, not prevention: do not claim that the audit can stop another live session from writing .git/config. Evidence: the current audit only rejects known agent identities, while a human repo-local identity silently passes; five live sessions share the config. This is the R1 disposition. This is the corrected successor of shared-clone-git-identity-drift-guard-v1; its stored rung was repaired during adversarial plan review.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not claim the warning prevents writes by another agent.
anti_patterns.instead: State the detection-only boundary in the code, tests, and AGENTS.md rule.
anti_patterns.why: The audit runs after configuration may already have changed.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not edit the shared .git/config or global Git configuration as part of this PR.
anti_patterns.instead: Make the audit and AGENTS.md warning visible, then use per-command git -c identity overrides.
anti_patterns.why: The shared clone is used by multiple live sessions and direct repair is itself the race the item is addressing.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not make every human repo-local identity fatal.
anti_patterns.instead: Emit a non-fatal warning for any repo-local user.* and retain fatal status only for disallowed identities.
anti_patterns.why: That would turn a visibility guard into a compatibility break and obscure the known-agent safety check.

preserves.behavior: Known Claude/agent/service identities remain fatal unless the existing explicit override is used.
Normal per-commit git -c user.name=... -c user.email=... workflow remains supported.
The audit remains non-mutating and does not attempt to prevent concurrent config writes.

verifications.description: Unfixed-tree gate: the real JSON audit CLI must emit a non-fatal repo-local identity warning for injected human user.* values; current develop has no warnings field/value.
verifications.expected: FAIL on unfixed develop: the human repo-local identity is silently accepted and JSON has no warning; exits 1 before the guard and 0 after it.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'import importlib.util,os; from pathlib import Path; env={"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT":"2","GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0":"user.name","GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0":"Claude","GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1":"user.email","GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1":"noreply@anthropic.com"}; os.environ.update(env); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("audit","_project/scripts/agent_instruction_audit.py"); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); errors=m.audit_git_identity(Path(".")); assert len(errors)==2 and all("known agent/service" in e for e in errors), errors; os.environ["BENCHBOX_ALLOW_AGENT_GIT_IDENTITY"]="1"; assert m.audit_git_identity(Path("."))==[]'

verifications.expected: PASS on current develop and after the change: known agent rejection and explicit override behavior remain intact.
